title: Two photon imaging of calcium responses in murine Purkinje neurons
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse in an induction chamber with a flow of 2 L/min oxygen and 2% isoflurane.
Make vertical incisions starting from bregma along the sagittal suture until reaching the junction between the cortex and the cerebellum.
Cut laterally towards both sides of the skull as indicated by the dashed white lines.
Make two small incisions below the lateral most side of cerebellum.
Grasp the back of skull flap with forceps and lift outward and upward to remove the skull that covers the cerebellum.
Monitor the level of anesthesia throughout the experiment using the pedal withdrawal reflex to toe pinch.
If a pedal reflex is observed during toe pinching, conclude that the animal is not fully anesthetized.
Keep the animal in the chamber for additional time until fully anesthetized.
Anesthetize mice using 1 mL of isoflurane applied onto a paper towel inside a chamber.
Place a grid above the paper towel to avoid direct contact between isoflurane and mouse skin.
Cut the skin from the back of the skull to the top to expose the skull.
Make a hole at the bregma level using mini bone rongeurs or fine scissors.
Use small scissors to make a rostral-to-caudal cut along the sagittal suture starting from bregma level.
Continue cutting the skull laterally towards both sides after reaching the junction between cortex and cerebellum.
Make two small incisions below the lateral most side of cerebellum carefully avoiding tissue damage.
Use forceps to grasp the back of the skull flap.
Lift the skull flap outward and upward to remove the skull covering the cerebellum.
Place the severed head directly onto ice-cold ACSF sucrose solution immediately after decapitation.
Cool the brain by placing it into cold ACSF-Sucrose for approximately 2 minutes.
Transfer the cooled brain onto a Petri dish containing oxygenated, cold ACSF-Sucrose continuously bubbled with carbogen.
Use scissors to cut the optic nerves of the extracted brain.
Dissect out the cerebellum from the extracted brain using Scalpel blade No.13.
Glue the dissected cerebellum onto the agar block using cyanoacrylate Instant Adhesive (Evobond Super Glue – SG0312).
Position the cerebellum adhered to the agar block so that the flocculonodular lobe is parallel to the agar block and one of the lateral sides touches the vibratome table.
Add glue at the bottom of the cerebellum that touches the vibratome table and a small portion of the flocculo-nodular lobe to ensure adherence during sectioning.
Use a flat spatula to transfer the cerebellum onto the agar block.
Dry the cerebellum lightly on a piece of paper before gluing to prevent detachment from the agar block and vibratome table.
Immerse vibratome table containing the cerebellum into the vibratome tray filled with ice-cold ACSF-Sucrose bubbled continuously with carbogen.
Set the speed of the vibratome to 0.16 mm/s and the amplitude to 1.0 mm.
Adjust the angle of the blade so that the cutting edge is aligned parallel to the top of the mounted cerebellum.
Obtain parasagittal cerebellar slices of approximately 250 μm thickness at a temperature of about 1°C.
Use a vibratome cooler or place ice around the vibratome tray to maintain the temperature at 1°C during sectioning.
Transfer the cerebellar slices onto a bath containing oxygenated ACSF-Recovery solution maintained at 34°C using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Place the cerebellum in a vibratome tray filled with ice-cold ACSF-Sucrose.
Maintain the temperature around the vibratome tray at approximately 1°C during sectioning.
Keep cerebellar slices in oxygenated ACSF-Recovery solution in a water bath maintained at 34°C.
Hold cerebellar slices in an incubation chamber using a nylon mesh.
Place the cerebellar slice on a nylon mesh fitted to the beaker for adequate oxygenation of the slices.
Leave cerebellar slices in oxygenated ACSF-Recovery bath at 34°C for 45 minutes.
Incubate the slices for 45 minutes to recover.
Transfer the slices onto a brain slice holding chamber containing oxygenated ACSF-Normal solution maintained at room temperature (∼22°C).
Fit a beaker with nylon netting and attach a tube for carbogen gas flow.
Control the rate of carbogen gas flow to prevent floating of brain slices in the chamber.
Place acute cerebellar slices one at a time into the recording chamber.
Keep the recording chamber under a custom-built two-photon laser scanning microscope equipped with a Ti-Sapphire laser (Coherent Chameleon Ultra II).
Use a 20× water-immersion objective (Olympus XLUMPLFLN20XW, 1.0 NA) for imaging.
Use a glass Pasteur pipette to transfer cerebellar slices onto a recording chamber containing oxygenated ACSF-Normal solution maintained at room temperature.
Continuously perfuse the bath in the recording chamber with oxygenated ACSF-normal at room temperature.
Check the flow of carbogen gas in the holding chamber frequently to prevent slices from floating and to avoid air bubbles near the slices.
Place a slice anchor gently onto the cerebellar slices in the recording chamber.
Locate the cells of interest using the “focus” button in Scan Image 3.8.
Define a region that includes Purkinje neuron soma and dendrites for scanning.
Set the two photon laser at minimal power to avoid phototoxicity while ensuring baseline green fluorescence is visible.
Acquire the fluorescence of each cell in time lapse mode with acquisition time per frame set to 1 second.
Capture images with a size of 512 x 512 pixels.
Add 75 mM KCl at the 10th frame for depolarization.
Continue capturing images for 120 seconds after adding KCl.
Stimulate Purkinje neurons with approximately 200 μM DHPG in ACSF solution starting from the 10th frame of image acquisition.
Capture images for 600 seconds after adding DHPG.
Apply an mGluR1 antagonist, CPCCOEt, at a concentration of 200 μM to the neurons before stimulating with DHPG.
Add 200 μM CPCCOEt to the bath solution in recording chamber before image acquisition.
Add 200 μM DHPG to the solution at the 10th frame of image acquisition after applying CPCCOEt.
Select healthy neurons that are 50 μm below the superficial surface.
Continuously perfuse the bath in recording chamber with oxygenated ACSF-normal at room temperature.
Stop image acquisition when neurons show signs of deteriorating health such as enlarged soma, increase in basal GCaMP6f fluorescence, blebbing and fragmentation of dendrites.
Incubate slices with 200 μM CPCCOEt.
Stimulate Purkinje neurons with KCl and record changes in GCaMP6f fluorescence.
Stimulate Purkinje neurons with DHPG and record changes in GCaMP6f fluorescence.
